name: qodercli-for-vscode
description: Run the Qoder CLI coding agent in a VS Code terminal — it automatically sees your live editor context: active file, cursor line, selected code, and open files. No @file typing, no copy-paste.

commands.title: Qoder CLI: Open Editor Context Settings File

qoder.executablePath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to the CLI executable. When left empty, `qodercli` is looked up automatically from `PATH` first, then the `qoder` dispatcher, then the default install locations (`~/.local/bin/qodercli`, `~/.qoder/bin/qodercli/qodercli`, `~/.qoder/entry/qoder`).

qoder.injectEditorContext.markdownDescription: Automatically pass `--settings <deployed settings file>` when launching the Qoder CLI terminal so editor context is injected. Disable it if your CLI build does not support `--settings`, or if you want to load your own settings file via `#qoder.launchArgs#`. The deployed settings file (with the `UserPromptSubmit` hook) can be opened with the **Qoder CLI: Open Editor Context Settings File** command so you can merge the hook into your own settings.

qoder.launchArgs.markdownDescription: Extra arguments appended to the Qoder CLI launch command, after any automatically injected arguments. Many CLIs take the last occurrence of a repeated flag, so a `--settings` added here usually wins; if your CLI rejects duplicate flags, turn off `#qoder.injectEditorContext#`. Supported variables: `${settingsPath}` (deployed settings file) and `${hookPath}` (deployed hook script). Example: `["--settings", "${settingsPath}", "--verbose"]`.
